name: Royal Pine Apartments
headline: DBG Properties of Portland, Oregon, is building Royal Pine Apartments, 232 new one- to three-bedroom homes for households at 30% to 70% AMI in three four-story buildings at 4150 Royal Pine Dr in Colorado Springs' Briargate area, with a 2023-cycle federal 4% credit and City of Colorado Springs bonds.
why_it_matters: A rare affordable deal in high-cost north Colorado Springs that survived neighbor opposition and a lawsuit; the delay voided the 2023 bond authority and forced a new $60M bond ordinance in 2025 using the city's banked bond cap.

status.label: Under construction (permits pulled November 2025); completion targeted July 2027
status.detail: The Pikes Peak Regional Building Department issued permits in November 2025 and reported the project under construction on 2025-11-21. City presentations in May 2025 targeted completion by 2027-07-31. No financing closing date was found in public records.

next_step: Watch Pikes Peak Regional Building Department inspections and a certificate of occupancy around mid-2027.

key_numbers.meaning: 124 one-, 64 two- and 44 three-bedroom units; 17 at 30%, 164 at 60% and 51 at 70% AMI using income averaging (average 60% AMI, computed).
Federal credit runs 10 years; amounts marked subject to change.

key_numbers.value: $39,575,000 in City of Colorado Springs bonds
key_numbers.meaning: Amount on CHFA's report; City Council authorized up to $60M in May 2025 after a 2023 authority of up to $40M expired.
Cash-flow loan from the State Housing Board (October 2024).

background.text: City staff presented the project at a 2023-05-22 council work session, describing income averaging and a city plan to use most of its 2023 bond allocation; DBG Properties had earlier built Academy Heights in the city.

On 2023-06-13 City Council voted 7-2 for an inducement resolution declaring intent to issue up to $40M of private activity bonds, over objections from Pine Creek neighbors about density, traffic, water and wildlife.
Neighbors said city mailings in June 2023 did not mention an apartment complex; the city said multifamily was always an allowed use on the parcel.
The planning commission approved the development plan in early 2024 and City Council, at a February 2024 special meeting, allowed the project to proceed.

A neighborhood group sued the city in 2023; El Paso County District Court dismissed the case (reported as January 2025), and a federal court recommended remand to the county court in April 2025. The delay caused the 2023 bond resolution to expire.
On 2025-05-13 City Council passed the final ordinance authorizing up to $60M of bonds, 8-1; the city is a conduit issuer and is not liable for repayment.
The deal does not appear in CHFA's 2023 Round One or Round Two applicant reports or the 2023 Round Two award report.
